title: Product law from singleton factorization
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $p$ be a deterministic protocol for disjointness on inputs of length $n$, and let $z$ be an achievable value of its summary $Z=(M,T,X_{<T},Y_{>T})$. Let $\mu$ be the conditional law of the special-bit pair $(X_T,Y_T)$ on the fiber $Z=z$, and let $\mu_X$ and $\mu_Y$ be the corresponding conditional laws of its two coordinates. If, for every $b=(b_1,b_2)\in\{0,1\}^2$, the real mass $\mu(\{b\})$ equals $\mu_X(\{b_1\})\mu_Y(\{b_2\})$, then $\mu=\mu_X\otimes\mu_Y$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a deterministic length-$n$ disjointness protocol
singleton-mass factorization holds for every Boolean pair
replaced:
Fix a positive integer $n$ and a deterministic disjointness protocol $p$ on inputs of
length $n$, and let $z$ be an achievable value of the variable $Z=(M,T,X_{<T},Y_{>T})$.
Write $\mu$ for the conditional law, on the fiber $\{Z=z\}$, of the special bit-pair
$(X_T,Y_T)\in\{0,1\}^2$, and write $\mu_X$ and $\mu_Y$ for the conditional laws on that
same fiber of the individual special bits $X_T$ and $Y_T$. Suppose that for every pair
$b=(b_1,b_2)\in\{0,1\}^2$ the mass assigned by $\mu$ to the singleton $\{b\}$ equals the
product $\mu_X(\{b_1\})\,\mu_Y(\{b_2\})$. Then $\mu$ is the product measure
$\mu_X\otimes\mu_Y$.
